Title: Persona
Text: Bhavin, co-founder & lead seller. Sells between meetings and on the road; owns FinEdge $95k, NovaPharma $80k, ShopSwift $55k, Meridian $45k.

Title: Root cause
Text: AtliQ does not lack leads; it lacks memory. Client asks, promises, deadlines, referrals and revisit dates live in emails, calls and notes, never in the CRM, so nobody can see what is owed to whom and by when.

Title: Evidence
Text: 0/40 CRM records have a next follow-up date; 21 have no value; 5 no owner; Meridian duplicated; 4+ email leads and ~11 TechSummit contacts never entered; ~$470k of valued pipeline waiting on an overdue AtliQ action (as of 10 Jul 2026).

Title: Goal
Text: Find where AI genuinely helps a founder-seller remember and act, score it, and scope a safe MVP for the PRD.

Title: S9 Pipeline review & prioritisation | AI opportunities
O1 Link conversations to accounts
Text: Match every email, note and quick note to the right CRM account by company, contact email and lead_id; flag duplicates. Why AI: Fuzzy matching of messy names ("Meridian Health LLC" vs "Meridian Healthcare") is a language task; the join keys exist in the dataset. Evidence: Meridian L-1003/L-1027; GlobalMart L-1004/L-1040 Stage: S1-S2

Title: O2 Commitment & ask ledger
Text: Extract client asks, AtliQ promises, deadlines, budget and stakeholders from each thread, with a citation to the source line. Why AI: Core LLM strength: structured extraction from unstructured text. Every item can be grounded in a quoted source. Evidence: FinEdge call slot, Meridian questions, ShopSwift SOW 15 Jul, NovaPharma 24 Jul, Zenlytics invite Stage: S3-S5

Title: O3 Daily "what needs me today" brief
Text: Per-seller list ranked by due date, days waiting and deal value, each item linked to its source. Why AI: Ranking is transparent rules on top of O2 output; AI writes the short why-it-matters line. Depends on O2 quality. Evidence: "We find out what's urgent by accident" (Karandeep); HealthFirst 14 Jul found by search Stage: S4-S6, S9

Title: O4 Draft new leads from unseen contacts
Text: When a conversation involves a company not in the CRM, draft a lead (company, contact, source, referrer, interest) for approval. Why AI: Needs entity extraction plus an "is this new?" check against the CRM; easy for a human to verify. Evidence: Harbor & Finch (FinEdge referral), Nimbus Lending (PayTrack), PixelWorks, Lumino Fitness Stage: S1-S2

Title: O5 Proposed CRM updates (one-tap approve)
Text: Suggest status, owner, next follow-up date and value changes with the evidence; seller approves or edits. Why AI: Inferring a field value from a conversation is risky if auto-written, safe with approval. Evidence: Trustline "Proposal Sent" vs approved; ClearPath "Lost" vs re-engaging; 0/40 follow-up dates Stage: S2, S6, S8, S9

Title: O6 Revisit & cross-sell radar
Text: Spot "check back in Q_", budget-unfrozen, second-problem and referral signals; surface them on the right date. Why AI: Signals are implicit in prose ("does AtliQ also do the dashboard layer?"); rules can't catch them, an LLM can, with a citation. Evidence: Northwind dashboards, PayTrack merchant-risk, Acme automation, ClearPath, Kaveri, Quantia Q2 2026 Stage: S7-S8

Title: O7 Reply & follow-up drafts
Text: Draft a reply that answers the open ask using only facts in AtliQ's records; seller edits and sends. Why AI: LLM drafting is mature; the risk is invented prices or dates, so drafts must cite and leave gaps blank. Evidence: FinEdge slot reply, ClearPath "does the 40k estimate still hold?", Sunrise Foods v2 call Stage: S5, S7

Title: O8 Voice / text quick capture from phone
Text: Seller speaks or types a 20-second note after a call; AI structures it into the ledger and links the account. Why AI: Speech-to-text plus extraction is mature; needs a mobile surface, which adds build effort for a prototype. Evidence: "I answer emails on my phone ... by the time I'm at a laptop it's gone" Stage: S1, S3

Title: O9 Business-card scan to lead
Text: Photo of a conference card becomes a draft lead. Why AI: OCR works, but cards are not in the dataset and volume is a few events a year. Evidence: ~15 TechSummit cards, 4 entered Stage: S1

Title: O10 Pipeline review pack
Text: Auto-generated pre-meeting pack: overdue items, unowned deals, missing leads, CRM gaps. Why AI: A different view of O2-O5 output; little new AI work. Saves Jay's ~2 hours. Evidence: 2 Jul review: 2 hours reconciling and still gaps Stage: S9

Title: O11 Win-probability / lead scoring
Text: Predict which deals will close. Why AI: 40 records and no outcome history: a model would be guessing. Not where the pain is. Evidence: Pain is forgetting, not choosing (Step 1 root cause) Stage: S6

Title: O12 Auto-send follow-ups
Text: Email clients automatically when something is overdue. Why AI: Technically easy, but one wrong price or tone on a $95k deal outweighs the time saved. Founders own the relationship. Evidence: Founder-led sales; relationships are the asset Stage: S5

Title: O13 Auto-write proposals / SOWs
Text: Generate full SOWs and pricing. Why AI: No pricing or past-SOW corpus in the dataset; high risk of invented scope and price. Evidence: ShopSwift SOW due 15 Jul Stage: S4

Title: O14 Auto-answer security questionnaires
Text: Fill the 78-question NovaPharma questionnaire. Why AI: Needs a verified security knowledge base AtliQ hasn't got; wrong answers create legal exposure. Better: flag it and get an owner assigned. Evidence: NovaPharma questionnaire, forwarded to Pranav, untouched Stage: S4

Title: O15 Web enrichment of contacts
Text: Scrape LinkedIn / the web to fill contact fields. Why AI: Privacy and terms-of-service risk; the grounded-only principle says stay inside AtliQ's own records. Evidence: Missing contacts for Ridgeline, BlueOrchid, CargoLine Stage: S2

Title: Scoring rubric
Text: Impact (1-5): revenue at risk + how often it happens + strength of dataset evidence. Feasibility (1-5): data available in the dataset + maturity of the AI technique + cost of being wrong + prototype build effort. Score = Impact x Feasibility (max 25). Do first = Impact >= 4 and Feasibility >= 4.

Title: F1 Capture & Link
Text: From: O1, O4 | AI capability: Entity extraction + fuzzy entity resolution (LLM + string similarity on company, email domain, lead_id) | Inputs: Email threads, meeting notes, CRM export | Output: Each source linked to an account; duplicate flags; draft leads for unseen companies | Guardrails: Never merges records automatically; shows match confidence; below threshold it asks ("Meridian Healthcare or Meridian Health LLC?"); new leads are drafts only. | Human in loop: Seller confirms each link, merge and new lead | Test: Link accuracy over all 50 dataset files; must find the Meridian duplicate and the 4 missing email leads

Title: F2 Commitment & Signal Ledger
Text: From: O2, O6 | AI capability: Structured extraction to a fixed schema (type, who owes, to whom, due date, amount, quote) + date normalisation ("Q4", "mid-July") | Inputs: Linked sources from F1 | Output: One ledger row per ask, promise, deadline, revisit or cross-sell, each with a verbatim source quote | Guardrails: No quote, no item. Never invents dates or amounts; vague dates marked approximate. The dataset's editorial notes are used only as test ground truth, never as input. | Human in loop: Seller can dismiss or edit any item | Test: Recall and precision against a hand-labelled set of ~40 commitments; 0 items without a citation

Title: F3 Daily Brief ("What needs me today")
Text: From: O3, O10 | AI capability: Deterministic ranking (due date, days waiting, deal value) + LLM one-line summary per item | Inputs: Ledger (F2) + CRM owner and value | Output: Per-seller ranked list; review-pack view for the pipeline meeting; unowned items flagged | Guardrails: Ranking rules are transparent and shown; summaries only restate ledger facts; unknown owner shown as Unassigned, never guessed. | Human in loop: Seller assigns owners and snoozes items | Test: Bhavin's top 5 on 10 Jul must include FinEdge, ShopSwift, NovaPharma and Meridian

Title: F4 Propose, never act alone
Text: From: O5, O7 | AI capability: Field-value inference (status, owner, next follow-up) + grounded reply drafting | Inputs: Ledger + CRM record | Output: Suggested CRM changes with evidence; reply drafts with blanks for unknown facts | Guardrails: Nothing is written to the CRM or sent to a client without one-tap approval; drafts contain no price, date or commitment absent from the sources. | Human in loop: Approve, edit or reject every change and draft | Test: Suggestion approval rate; 0 invented facts in a reviewed sample of drafts

Title: Next (post-MVP)
Text: From: O8 | AI capability: Speech-to-text + the F2 extraction | Inputs: Phone voice or text note after a call | Output: Structured ledger items | Guardrails: Same as F2; audio not kept after transcription | Human in loop: Seller reviews the structured note | Test: Run once the MVP proves extraction quality

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Grounded only: every output cites a file and a quote from AtliQ's records.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Human in control: approval before anything changes a record or reaches a client.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Uncertainty is visible: confidence is shown; low confidence asks rather than guesses.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Least data: client data stays in AtliQ's workspace; no third-party enrichment; no training on client data.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Audit trail: every suggestion, approval and rejection is logged with who and when.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Fail safe: a source that can't be read or linked lands in an Unlinked inbox, never silently dropped.

Title: Risk: Wrong account link mixes two clients' facts
Text: Mitigation: Confidence threshold + human confirm; never auto-merge

Title: Risk: Missed commitment gives false comfort
Text: Mitigation: Measure recall on the labelled set; show a sources-scanned count

Title: Risk: Invented date or price in a draft
Text: Mitigation: Citation-required schema; drafts leave blanks; review before send

Title: Risk: Alert fatigue: the brief gets long and ignored
Text: Mitigation: Cap the top items per seller; snooze; rank by urgency x value

Title: Risk: Sellers don't adopt it (like the CRM)
Text: Mitigation: It gives back in the moment: the brief is the payoff and capture needs no typing

Title: Step 3 PRD
Text: Step 3 PRD: North Star candidate = % of client asks and AtliQ commitments actioned within 2 business days (today: FinEdge 21 days, Meridian 24, ClearPath 31). Supporting: pipeline completeness (owner + next step + follow-up date), extraction recall and precision, suggestion approval rate, hours of reconciliation before review.
